body:
# aggregator(actions): markResult caps split surrogate pairs — appliedByRun/resultNote stored with a lone surrogate (residual of #7694)

## Evidence (verified this run, main `83b7a024b8`)

#7694 fixed `cleanText` in `pm-stack/aggregator/src/actions.ts` so its caps never split a surrogate pair. The action-result path in the same file was not given the same guard — it caps with raw `slice`:

`pm-stack/aggregator/src/actions.ts:797-798` (`ActionsStore.markResultTransition`):

```ts
a.appliedByRun = result.byRun.slice(0, 200);
if (result.note) a.resultNote = result.note.slice(0, 2_000);
```

Both values are stored on the action record and persisted by `persist()` into the actions store file — the same stored-field corruption class as #7694, reached through the result route (`pm-stack/aggregator/src/server.ts:1236`, `POST /api/action-result`) instead of `validateNewAction`. `markResult` (`actions.ts:778`) delegates to `markResultTransition`, so both entry points are affected.

Probe (laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-actions-result-surrogate/probe.ts`, real `actions.ts` imported from the laptop primary at `83b7a024b8`, md5 `1485fa202f948031c9ea283fb8f25bfe`; `ActionsStore` over a temp file):

- `byRun` = `"r" × 199 + "😀" + "tail"` → stored `appliedByRun` is exactly 200 code units, last code unit `0xd83d` — a lone high surrogate. UTF-8 encode/decode round-trip differs and ends in U+FFFD.
- `note` = `"n" × 1999 + "😀" + "tail"` → stored `resultNote` is exactly 2,000 code units, last code unit `0xd83d` — same lone surrogate, same U+FFFD round-trip corruption.
- The persisted actions file literally contains the `\ud83d` escape.
- Control: `note` = `"n" × 1998 + "😀"` (exactly 2,000 code units, pair fits) is stored intact, length 2,000.

Dedup: #7694 (closed, fixed by PR #7698) covers only `cleanText` / `validateNewAction` payload fields; its acceptance criteria do not reach `markResultTransition`. Searches for `markResult` + surrogate and `resultNote` found no other filing.

## Why it matters

This is the exact defect class fixed three times now in sibling boundaries (#3178 for pm-dispatch, #7694 for action payloads): a cap counted in UTF-16 code units silently halves an astral character, and the lone surrogate is then persisted and delivered to downstream consumers — UTF-8 encoders corrupt it to U+FFFD, and strict parsers (e.g. Rust `serde_json`) reject unpaired surrogates outright. A result reported by a run whose id or note happens to place an emoji at the 200 / 2,000 boundary corrupts the audit record for that action.

## Acceptance criteria

- `markResultTransition` never stores an `appliedByRun` or `resultNote` ending in a lone high surrogate: when a cap would split a surrogate pair, the pair is dropped whole (stored length `max - 1` code units for that value), reusing or mirroring the #7694 `cleanText` guard.
- Cap semantics otherwise identical: same maximum code-unit lengths (200 / 2,000), no trim or empty-handling changes, non-straddling values byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Regression tests in `pm-stack/aggregator/test/actions.test.ts`: an astral character straddling both the `byRun` (200) and `note` (2,000) caps is stored whole-or-dropped, never halved; an exact-fit pair at the cap is kept whole; the new tests fail on the pre-fix code.
- Existing aggregator actions suite stays green.
